For what it's worth, I'm not convinced the cause explains the effect. European markets are also down [1].

[1] https://www.cnbc.com/markets/europe-markets/

comment_text.value:
Frankly if I was China, I'd be conflicted about the mid-terms - Trump is currently leading the US to disastrous wars - kinetic and trade, pissing off his closest allies, under-mining the dollar, and making China look a sane and stable partner.

On the other hand the world might be better off if he was more constrained post mid-terms.

Frankly, in terms of countries wanting Trump to take a beating in the mid-terms, I'd put countries like Canada and most of Europe way ahead of China there.

And in terms of China's energy strategy - China is the worlds biggest net importer of crude therefore China's strategy is going to be focussed on managing that first and foremost.

I think it's the US who hoped that the oil crisis would impact China much more - this is the US making, not China.

story_title.value: Houthis 'take control' of key island in global shipping route

comment_text.value:
> He literally says he'll cut a check for $5,000 for every adult american if the Republicans win both the House and Senate in the midterms.

Which is exactly why it doesn't apply. The money would go to even the people who didn't vote for him.

The law you're referring to is about paying people for votes. Someone giving their own money to voters who can prove they cast a ballot in a particular way.

Saying that you're going to have taxpayer-funded transfer payments is ordinary politics. If your interpretation was right then proposing to increase social assistance programs would be vote buying in violation of that law.
